note: THE APPLICATIONS ANYUSE RECOGNISES. A map travels only if its app identity
MATCHES an entry here. Nothing else travels — not anonymised, not hashed,
not partly. A hash of a tenant identity is still a tenant correlator.
WHY A LIST AT ALL. Every earlier rule asked where a name came from and
trusted the answer. Twice the answer was honest and the name was still the
customer: the watcher built an 'OS app name' out of a window title
('Electron (Angebot Mueller GmbH)'), and the observing model reported a
screen as the application ('Angebot Mueller GmbH - Kalkulation'). Anything
derived from a running machine can be customer content, so identity is no
longer derived. It is matched against this file.
'identity' holds the EXACT names the operating system reports for that
application on the platforms anyuse watches (macOS today; SAP is listed
under its Windows launcher name too, because the same screens sit behind
it). Matching is exact after one normalisation — strip, casefold — and
nothing else. No substring, no prefix, no fuzz. A near-match is a
non-match: 'Microsoft Excel - Kunde Mueller GmbH' matches nothing here.
'application' is the name that TRAVELS, and it must also appear in
'identity'. The observed string is never copied onto a map; this one is
sent instead, so the single free-text identity on the wire comes out of
this file and never out of a screen. It is also what merges two tenants'
maps: 'SAP Logon' and 'SAP GUI' are one identity, so they share a handle.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Runtimes and shells that many different
applications report themselves as — Electron, node, helper, python, java,
javaw, wine — identify no vendor application, and an entry for one would
let every in-house app built on it travel under a vendor's name. Adding
them would make this list a wish, not a claim.
EXTENDING IT. Edit this file (or point ANYUSE_VENDOR_APPLICATIONS at
another one) and restart nothing — it is re-read when it changes. Add an
application only when you can name the vendor and the exact string the OS
reports for it. A list that cannot be read recognises nothing, and then
nothing travels.
